Subject: Bitfield on-prem deployment: operational runbook & initial requirements

Tyler —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching an initial requirements matrix that maps your site constraints to recommended cluster topology and operational controls. High-level asks in this note:

- Confirm rack space & power per rack (U and kW) and whether you can provision a 2U for a 2-node control-plane (if we go HA we prefer 3x 2U controllers).
- Confirm preferred storage for long-term model artifacts (NFS/S3-compatible object store or SAN).
- Network — do you allow BGP peering from our jump hosts, or will we need an outbound-only NAT approach?

Key recommendations captured in the matrix (attachment: bitfield_requirements_matrix.xlsx):
- Cluster footprint: 3 control-plane (HA) + 6 worker nodes (split into gpu-high and cpu-standard nodepools).
- Storage tiers: local NVMe scratch for ephemeral model cache; replicated persistent volumes (CSI LVM on top of SAN/NVMe) for model weights; object storage for archival.
- Networking: separate management Vlan for control plane and admin access; SR-IOV for low-latency inference NICs if available.
- K8s defaults to use volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer for GPU workloads to ensure correct node selection and topologies.

Please review the matrix and reply with the site-specific numbers for racks/power/networking. If useful, I can schedule a follow-up technical workshop with Dev and Soojin next week to lock down the runbook.

Camila

Camila —

Appreciate the thorough summary. Quick answers inline:

- Rack & Power: We have two 42U racks in the AI room with ~8 kW available per rack right now; we can free up an additional 2U if needed.
- Storage: Primary preference is a SAN (Dell PowerStore) with iSCSI LUNs; we also have an S3-compatible appliance (MinIO) for object storage.
- Network: No BGP peering allowed — outbound-only with static egress ranges and firewall rules is the model.
- SR-IOV: Not currently configured, but blueprints for Mellanox cards are available if you recommend it.

I'll attach the facility checklist in my next reply with rack elevations and power panel IDs. For the runbook, the team is particularly interested in the model cache behavior and node eviction tolerance during model loads.

On 2026-10-04 at 12:30, Tyler Nguyen wrote:
> - Rack & Power: We have two 42U racks in the AI room with ~8 kW available per rack right now; we can free up an additional 2U if needed.
> - Storage: Primary preference is a SAN (Dell PowerStore) with iSCSI LUNs; we also have an S3-compatible appliance (MinIO) for object storage.
> - Network: No BGP peering allowed — outbound-only with static egress ranges and firewall rules is the model.

Thanks Tyler — this helps. A few technical notes so the runbook and preflight checklist are actionable: 

1) Control plane topology: Given you prefer two racks with limited extra U, we should provision a 3x control-plane HA setup split across both racks (1+2) to avoid single-rack failure. Use anti-affinity for control-plane pods and enable etcd snapshotting to an external object store (MinIO) every 6 hours.

2) Node pools & labels:
   - gpu-high: 4x nodes, each with 4x A100 equivalent or nearest available; node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=gpu-high, redwood.inference/node-role=inference
   - cpu-standard: 2x nodes for batch jobs and control-plane-adjacent workloads; taint the gpu-high nodes to schedule GPU workloads only.

3) Storage guidance for SAN:
   - Use a CSI driver that supports volumes on top of iSCSI (rbd or csi-iscsi if validated for your PowerStore).
   - For model weights, create a replicated PVC class with encryption-at-rest (KMS) and read-only mounts for inference pods to allow safe multi-pod sharing.
   - Implement a local NVMe scratch class using local volume provisioner for /tmp model cache; set reclaimPolicy=Retain for debugging windows but configure lifecycle job to garbage collect older caches.

4) Network & egress:
   - Because you require outbound-only, we'll use a pair of NAT gateways in the management Vlan and pre-authorize Redwood egress ranges in your firewall.
   - For low-latency NICs without SR-IOV, use tuning at the OS and CNI layer: jumbo frames, tc qdisc tweaks, and CPU pinning for inference pods. If you enable SR-IOV later, we can add an alternate CNI profile.

5) Kubelet & eviction tuning:
   - kube-reserved and system-reserved must be sized to avoid OOM when model loading spikes.
   - Set eviction thresholds for ephemeral storage to 10% and configure a pod priority class for in-flight inference to avoid cascading evictions.

6) Runbook items I will draft for the workshop: preflight checklist (power, networking ACLs, DNS), node provisioning playbook (PXE or image), storage provisioning & snapshot schedule, cluster restore procedures, and in-field troubleshooting playbook for model loading stalls.

I'll attach a short ops checklist to the repo after the weekend. Camila — can you schedule the workshop? I suggest a 90-minute technical session with site ops to walk rack elevations and the SAN mapping.

— Dev
